item.title: EHang opens Thailand hub for Southeast Asia eVTOL rollout
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: EHang has established a Thailand hub and plans an initial fleet of 25 EH216-S aircraft to support eVTOL projects across Southeast Asia.
item.content:encoded:
China’s EHang has established an overseas regional hub in Thailand to support electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft projects across Southeast Asia and other emerging markets.

The Nasdaq-listed company said it plans to deploy an initial fleet of 25 EH216-S pilotless passenger-carrying aircraft in Thailand. The aircraft would support flight validation, operational preparation and project implementation across regional markets.

Thailand becomes a regional deployment base

EHang said the hub will position aircraft and other resources closer to projects, allowing it to coordinate deployments across countries. The company did not disclose the investment required for the hub, its exact location, staffing or a delivery schedule for the 25 aircraft.

The announcement extends EHang’s existing work in Thailand. In its second-quarter results, the company said it was conducting local flight validation and preparing for commercial operations under a regulatory sandbox with the Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand.

EHang launched that sandbox initiative in Bangkok in October 2025 and has described Thailand as a potential model for entry into other markets. Commercial passenger operations have not been approved, and any service would still require local certification, safety assessments and operating authorization.

The Thailand base will support EHang’s passenger mobility, aerial logistics, emergency-response and aerial-media products. EHang said it has already deployed about 1,200 GD4.0 formation drones in Thailand for light shows and plans to expand that fleet to more than 10,000 units. Those fleet figures and the expansion target are company-supplied.

Company outlines near-term regional tests

EHang also set out several planned milestones across Asia. It expects sandbox launch and validation flights at Port City Colombo in Sri Lanka in November, with commercial operations targeted by the end of 2026 under the local sandbox framework.

In Vietnam, the company expects validation flights within Hanoi’s sandbox area in November. TNGlobal previously reported that Hanoi and local partner HungViet agreed to pursue controlled testing of the EH216-S at Hoa Lac High-Tech Park. That work remains subject to Vietnam’s application and approval process.

EHang is also preparing an initial EH216-S demonstration in Putrajaya, Malaysia, after announcing sandbox cooperation with the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia in October. In Thailand, it plans to demonstrate the aircraft during an International Civil Aviation Organization advanced-air-mobility symposium in Bangkok in December.

The timelines are not firm launch commitments. EHang said the deployments, validation flights, demonstrations and potential operations remain subject to local laws, operational preparation, safety assessments and regulatory approvals.

Regulatory execution remains central

The new hub gives EHang a physical coordination point for its regional expansion, but it does not itself authorize passenger flights. Aviation regulators in each market will determine whether and how the pilotless aircraft can operate.

EHang’s EH216-S has obtained type, production and standard airworthiness certificates from the Civil Aviation Administration of China. Those Chinese certifications provide a technical reference, but they do not replace local approvals in Thailand or other Southeast Asian markets.

The company’s regional plans therefore hinge on turning sandbox tests into operating permissions while building local maintenance, training and safety systems. EHang has said its strategy is to standardize that process so it can be repeated across markets.

EHang-backed Hanoi sandbox to test pilotless aircraft taxi

item.title: IBS plans HK$563M acquisition of AI chip company
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Hong Kong-listed IBS has agreed to acquire QuantumCompute Solutions for HK$563 million in a conditional move into AI chip design and edge computing.
item.content:encoded:
Hong Kong-listed International Business Settlement Holdings Limited has agreed to acquire the entire equity interest in QuantumCompute Solutions Limited for HK$563 million ($72.4 million), in a conditional transaction that would add artificial intelligence chip design and edge-computing capabilities to the group.

The company, known as IBS, entered into the share purchase agreement with seller Brainwave Innovations Limited on October 30, according to its listed-company announcement. The deal remains subject to conditions and a restructuring of the target group. QuantumCompute would become a wholly owned IBS subsidiary when the acquisition is completed.

Target group centers on edge AI chips

QuantumCompute is an investment holding company that indirectly controls Shanghai Tianjing Fulian, an operating business focused on the design and development of AI system-on-chip products and integrated solutions. The business targets low-power AI inference and edge-computing applications, according to the announcement.

IBS said QuantumCompute will indirectly hold about 85.94 percent of Shanghai Tianjing Fulian after a required internal restructuring. Foxconn Industrial Internet separately owns 5.56 percent of the Shanghai company, the announcement said.

The restructuring is a condition precedent to completion. It will place Shanghai Tianjing Fuyu under Tianjing Fulian (Tianjin) and increase Shanghai Tianjing Fuyu’s interest in Shanghai Tianjing Fulian from about 70.28 percent to approximately 85.94 percent.

The ownership chain includes several recently formed holding vehicles. QuantumCompute was incorporated in the British Virgin Islands in June 2026, Neuro Link was incorporated in Hong Kong in July, and Tianjing Fulian (Tianjin) was established in China on October 27, according to the disclosure. Shanghai Tianjing Fuyu, established in 2023, is engaged in AI-chip research and development but remains at an early stage without material operations. Shanghai Tianjing Fulian is identified as the target group’s main operating entity.

The company said Shanghai Tianjing Fulian is an authorized independent chip design house for MediaTek. That status and other product or technology claims are company-supplied and were not independently quantified in the announcement.

IBS seeks to broaden its technology portfolio

IBS currently has businesses spanning fintech-related services and computing-power infrastructure. Its board said the acquisition is intended to move the group further into AI chip design and edge-computing infrastructure while reducing its exposure to cryptocurrency-market volatility.

The buyer plans to continue operating the target’s principal businesses as a standalone operation after completion. IBS also said it does not currently intend to terminate or materially reduce its existing business segments.

The board expects the target’s chip-design capabilities and industry network to create links with the group’s computing infrastructure and fintech businesses. Those expected synergies and growth benefits are forward-looking company assessments rather than completed operating results.

IBS said it has appointed semiconductor executive Tang Tianshen as chief strategic adviser for its fintech-related businesses and to advise on the target after completion. The company cited his previous roles at Intel, Shanghai Hua Hong and Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation as relevant experience. His appointment does not remove the execution and integration risks attached to the proposed acquisition.

The acquisition would give IBS access to the target’s personnel, technology assets and existing commercial relationships without building the capabilities internally. The buyer has not provided independently verified market-share, revenue or profitability figures for the chip business in the public release, so the transaction’s financial contribution cannot yet be assessed from those materials.

The transaction is classified as a discloseable transaction under Hong Kong listing rules. IBS also said it will change the use of part of the proceeds from an earlier share subscription to support the acquisition and related development. The Hong Kong exchange filing record lists the October 30 announcement.

Completion timing will depend on the agreement’s conditions, including the target-group restructuring. Until those requirements are met, QuantumCompute and the underlying chip business will remain outside IBS’s consolidated group.

China’s domestic AI stack gains momentum despite hardware gap

item.title: OMRON begins full-scale production at first India factory
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: OMRON Healthcare has started full-scale production at its first India factory near Chennai, targeting a tenfold capacity increase by 2028.
item.content:encoded:
OMRON Healthcare has begun full-scale production of blood pressure monitors at its first manufacturing site in India, expanding local supply while adding a new base to a network that has relied heavily on Vietnam.

The 24,000-square-meter plant near Chennai in Tamil Nadu has five production lines and will make devices for the Indian market, according to an OMRON Healthcare announcement published on Friday. The company said it intends to increase the site’s production capacity tenfold by 2028 and eventually use it to supply other markets.

India joins OMRON’s manufacturing network

OMRON established the Indian manufacturing company in July 2022 and began mass production in October 2026. The site had 120 employees as of November 2026, according to the company’s factory profile.

The first products include standard blood pressure monitors as well as models that can show changes in readings and connect with the OMRON Connect health-management app. OMRON said it has transferred production techniques and quality-control practices from plants in Japan and Vietnam to the Chennai operation.

Reuters reported that OMRON is targeting annual output of about 3 million units in India by 2028, with potential capacity of about 3.5 million units if the plant runs three shifts. The report said the factory will also supply Europe, supplementing production in Vietnam.

OMRON Healthcare President and Chief Executive Ayumu Okada told Reuters that India could become one of the company’s largest manufacturing bases. The move is also intended to reduce supply-chain risks created by concentrating production in one country or facility.

Company targets underpenetrated monitoring market

OMRON cited estimates that roughly 300 million people in India have hypertension while fewer than 5 percent of households use a blood pressure monitor at home. Those figures underscore the opportunity the company sees, but they are company-presented market estimates rather than independently audited operating data.

Reuters reported that OMRON held about 40 percent of India’s blood pressure monitor market in 2025. The company hopes home-monitor penetration will reach about 10 percent by 2030, although Okada said local production would not lead to lower device prices.

India is increasingly trying to build domestic medical-device capacity under the government’s Make in India program. OMRON said local sourcing, employee training and job creation at the Chennai plant would contribute to that policy objective.

For OMRON, the factory creates a base closer to a large potential market while diversifying its manufacturing footprint. It also gives the company room to add other products: OMRON said it may eventually produce nebulizers used in respiratory care at the site.

Expansion targets remain company plans

The plant is operational, but the 2028 capacity increase, European export role and additional product lines remain forward-looking. Their timing will depend on demand, supply-chain execution and any required approvals.

The launch is separate from OMRON Healthcare Singapore’s earlier embedded-health partnership with bolttech and QBE, which combined monitoring devices with insurance and subscription services.

OMRON Healthcare Singapore, bolttech, QBE team up to launch innovative embedded health solution

item.title: TPG closes debut Asia growth fund at $1.3B
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: TPG has closed its debut Asia lower-middle-market growth fund with $1.3 billion, exceeding the target for the new regional strategy.
item.content:encoded:
Global alternative asset manager TPG has completed fundraising for its first Asia lower-middle-market growth strategy with $1.3 billion in commitments, exceeding the target for the inaugural vehicle.

The firm disclosed the final size of TPG Emerging Companies Asia, or TECA, during its third-quarter earnings call on October 29. TPG said in its official earnings materials that the fund close was part of a broader quarter in which the group raised more than $15 billion across its strategies.

Fund targets developed Asia-Pacific markets

TECA is a lower-to-middle-market growth buyout strategy focused on developed Asia-Pacific markets, primarily Australia, New Zealand, Southeast Asia and South Korea, according to TPG’s regulatory filing.

The strategy targets profitable companies that TPG believes can benefit from regional growth trends. It is designed primarily for control-oriented transactions, while allowing selective minority investments.

TPG described the new strategy as an extension of its regional platform, which began investing in Asia in 1994. The firm’s Asia business had $23.6 billion in assets under management at the end of June 2026, with investment activity spanning Australia, India, Korea and Southeast Asia.

Within TPG, TECA sits in the firm’s Growth platform alongside strategies including TPG Growth, TPG Tech Adjacencies, TPG Life Sciences Innovations and TPG Sports. The structure gives the manager a dedicated vehicle for companies that are earlier in their development or smaller than the businesses usually considered for its flagship Capital platform.

Independent fund-market coverage reported that TECA had already deployed $338 million. Its initial investments include Singapore-based eldercare operators Orange Valley and Econ Healthcare, which have been combined under One Age Care, as well as Australian home-care provider Five Good Friends.

The close takes TECA above the $742 million in commitments that TPG had reported earlier in 2026. The final amount shows that the firm added substantial capital during the year despite a difficult fundraising environment for Asia-focused private-market vehicles.

Asia fund forms part of wider capital raising

TPG raised nearly $42 billion in the first nine months of 2026 and said it now expects full-year fundraising to exceed $55 billion. That is above its original $50 billion goal.

The asset manager ended September with approximately $346 billion in total assets under management, up 21 percent from a year earlier. Fee-paying assets under management reached $190 billion, while the group reported $86 billion of dry powder available for investment.

Alongside TECA, TPG completed or advanced fundraising across several other strategies during the quarter. It said TPG Capital X and Healthcare Partners III had attracted an additional $1.7 billion, while commitments to its third Tech Adjacencies fund reached $2.5 billion. Its Peppertree digital-infrastructure strategy had raised $2.2 billion through October.

The combination of regional sector teams and a growth-equity mandate allows TECA to pursue healthcare, business-services, technology and consumer opportunities at a different scale from TPG’s larger Asia funds. Actual portfolio construction will depend on the transactions the manager can source and complete, and the fund’s final geographic and sector mix has not been disclosed.

TPG’s chief executive described TECA as an example of the firm’s effort to build adjacent strategies around established investment platforms. For Asia, the vehicle adds a dedicated route to smaller profitable companies than those typically pursued by the firm’s flagship regional buyout funds.

The fund close comes as institutional investors remain selective about Asia-Pacific private equity. Large managers with established regional teams have continued to raise capital, while newer and smaller funds have generally faced longer fundraising cycles. TECA’s above-target close is therefore evidence of demand for TPG’s strategy, but it does not by itself indicate a broad recovery in regional fundraising.

Deployment will depend on suitable transactions in the fund’s target markets. TPG has not disclosed a schedule for investing the remaining capital, and the firm’s descriptions of opportunity and expected performance are forward-looking assessments.

Temasek and GIC acquire stake in Singapore-headquartered biotech specialist CRO Novotech

item.title: Coda, TikTok Gaming partnership brings Codashop purchases to creator videos across Southeast Asia
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Coda, a Singapore-headquartered digital content monetization and distribution company, has reached a partnership with TikTok Gaming to let users move from game content on the platform to purchases on Codashop, Coda's digital goods store, across Southeast Asia.
item.content:encoded:
Coda, a Singapore-headquartered digital content monetization and distribution company, has reached a partnership with TikTok Gaming to let users move from game content on the platform to purchases on Codashop, Coda’s digital goods store, across Southeast Asia.

In a statement on Friday, Coda said under the partnership, TikTok users in Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and the Philippines can link directly to Codashop to buy game top-ups, gift cards, and other digital goods. Creators can feature Codashop-listed content in livestreams and short-form videos. This can let publishers reach consumers where they already discover and engage with games.

Coda said that since its mid-June 2026 launch, creator videos linking to Codashop have drawn 1 billion views. It said click-through rates average above 5 percent. Around 5 percent of clicks convert to purchases, it added. Besides, most buyers are new to Codashop, which it presents as evidence that creator-led commerce can bring publishers new customers as well as transactions.

Zac Liew, chief commercial officer for business-to-business at Coda, said commerce increasingly happens wherever discovery happens. TikTok can give the company a new way to connect those moments, allowing publishers to reach consumers earlier and turn engagement into purchases.

Coda said the partnership reflects a broader shift in digital commerce, in which social platforms, creators, and contents play a growing role in consumer purchase decisions. It said the arrangement extends digital content distribution beyond traditional storefronts. The company said it will continue to explore commerce and distribution models with publishers and platform partners.

Roblox names Joel Neoh managing director for Southeast Asia, Oceania

item.title: NTU and Google deepen AI partnership
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (NTU Singapore) and Google are deepening their collaboration to accelerate artificial intelligence (AI) adoption across education, research, and workforce readiness.
item.content:encoded:
Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (NTU Singapore) and Google are deepening their collaboration to accelerate artificial intelligence (AI) adoption across education, research, and workforce readiness.

The partnership was formalized on Friday with the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding by NTU Provost and Deputy President, Professor Christian Wolfrum and Yossi Matias, Vice President, Google and General Manager, Google Research, NTU Singapore said in a statement.

Under the agreement, NTU and Google will explore initiatives across four key areas: campus-wide AI integration, regional language and sovereign model development under AI Singapore (AISG), frontier scientific research, and advanced AI safety. The partnership will also support faculty training, and professional certification.

The collaboration builds upon NTU’s existing partnership with Google as the University empowers its students to thrive in the age of AI. Since August 2026, NTU undergraduates have full access to a suite of premium Google AI tools, such as Gemini Enterprise, Google AI Studio, and Vertex AI.

”Our expanded partnership with Google provides our students, faculty, and researchers with access to frontier tools and secure cloud infrastructure. Embedding AI across NTU’s curriculum and research ecosystem provides a key differentiator in how we prepare our community for an AI-enabled future,

“By combining Google’s technological capabilities with NTU’s academic and scientific strengths, we can co-develop impactful applications, from preserving Southeast Asian languages to discovering new scientific insights, while upholding the highest standards of safety and responsibility,” said Professor Christian Wolfrum.

Yossi Matias said Singapore isn’t just adopting AI research – it is helping define how this technology serves science and society. “Sustaining that momentum requires long-term investment in local talent and a deep commitment to building responsibly. Our expanded partnership with NTU brings both together, giving Singapore’s researchers the resources to push scientific boundaries and turn breakthroughs into real-world impact in education and healthcare,” he said.

Under the new MOU, NTU and Google will expand AI enablement across teaching and research to support faculty, staff, and students. The education initiatives support NTU’s goal of embedding AI into 40 percent of undergraduate courses by 2030.

NTU will use Google AI tools to build capabilities among its faculty and educators through structured upskilling programs. Additionally, the University will explore integrating Gemini Enterprise with NTU Learn to turn pedagogical content into secure, searchable, and AI-accessible knowledge sources.

For example, educators could build AI assistants to guide students through course materials, or work with postgraduate researchers to turn research tasks into classroom activities. Students could use AI agents to compare evidence across papers or analyze a dataset, then explain and check the results themselves.

Professional development will be further supported by the Google AI Educator Series, offering stackable, badge-accredited training to build educator confidence and reduce administrative workload. Academic staff will also be able to attain Google for Education Certifications to validate digital literacy.

In partnership with AISG, NTU and Google will co-drive regional language initiatives that focus on collecting, cataloguing, and open-sourcing datasets that reflect Southeast Asian linguistic nuances, through Projects ATLAS and Amplify.

AISG will continue developing independent evaluation and benchmarking frameworks tailored to Southeast Asian cultural contexts for both frontier and open models.

Together, NTU and Google seek to develop sovereign AI models for education and healthcare that integrate Southeast Asian languages using Google’s open-weight models, such as Gemma and MedGemma.

To support advanced scientific discovery, NTU will design and deploy a secure research sandbox on Google Cloud Platform, developed with architectural guidance from Google.

The cloud sandbox will enable researchers to launch pre-approved environments on demand, reducing IT provisioning bottlenecks. The sandbox also provides potential access to Google’s latest AI technologies, serving as a secure shared space for joint projects with external research partners. For example, a research team could use AI and data-analysis tools in a pre-approved environment to examine a vetted dataset and share selected data with an authorized external collaborator, with permissions and data separation built in.

The partnership also opens up the possibility for academic research collaboration between NTU and Google Research in APAC, alongside ongoing initiatives with Google DeepMind.

NTU researchers can also gain early access to programs in relevant research areas, such as Google’s AI Hypothesis Generation system, which provides an accelerated channel to evaluate emerging AI capabilities for scientific discovery.

The agreement also encompasses research into AI privacy, safety, and security. Joint teams will investigate full-stack AI infrastructure protection that ensures data remains secure against future threats, focusing on post-quantum cryptography, deepfake detection, and cryptographic defenses for model privacy.

Singapore expands AI push through new national partnership with Google

item.title: Safran invests $152M to expand Malaysia aerospace operations
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: France-based aerospace firm Safran Landing Systems has invested a combined €136 million ($152 million) to expand its carbon brake manufacturing and refurbishment facility in Sendayan and establish a new maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) center in Nilai, as it seeks to meet growing demand from about 100 airline operators across the Asia-Pacific region.
item.content:encoded:
France-based aerospace firm Safran Landing Systems has invested a combined €136 million ($152 million) to expand its carbon brake manufacturing and refurbishment facility in Sendayan and establish a new maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) center in Nilai, as it seeks to meet growing demand from about 100 airline operators across the Asia-Pacific region.

The firm said in a statement on Wednesday that it inaugurated the expansion of its manufacturing and heat sink refurbishment facility in Sendayan, along with a new carbon brake Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) center in Nilai.  These complementary investments will help meet the growing needs of about 100 airline operators in Asia-Pacific, supporting fleets of Airbus (A320, A321, A350), Boeing (737, 777, 787) and ATR aircraft.

The €134 million expansion of the Sendayan facility adds 7,000 square meters of advanced manufacturing space, including a new textile line, carbonization furnaces and state-of-the-art machining equipment. The site, which currently employs 160 people, will double its carbon brake disc production capacity by 2028.

The new 1,000 square meter MRO center in Nilai represents an investment of €2 million. It is strategically located close to the Kuala Lumpur International Airport and 20 kilometers from Sendayan, which supplies it with new and refurbished carbon brake discs.

“Malaysia plays a strategic role in Safran Landing Systems’ global industrial footprint. Our investments in Sendayan and Nilai, combined with our local MRO partner network, reflect our commitment to supporting Asia Pacific’s long-term aviation growth by providing faster end-to-end wheels & brakes services, closer to our customers. They also demonstrate our dedication to developing local talent and reducing our environmental footprint,” said François Bastin, Safran Landing Systems Chief Executive Officer.

Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim Sikh Abdul Majid, CEO of the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA), said Safran has been present in Malaysia for more than 50 years, and the relationship has moved from supply and service into manufacturing, and now into maintenance, repair and overhaul.

“Expanding an existing plant and opening a new one in the same year is a strong confidence in Malaysia. These investments will create long-term value, develop high-skilled employment and further strengthen Malaysia’s aerospace capabilities,” he added.

To support this ramp-up, Safran Landing Systems plans to increase its workforce in Malaysia to 220 employees by 2030 across its industrial and MRO operations. This expansion will further strengthen the group’s capabilities in manufacturing, maintenance and customer support, while developing local skills and expertise.

Reflecting Safran’s environmental commitments, the Sendayan site has already reduced its greenhouse gas emissions by 60 percent between 2018 and 2025, by using low-carbon local energy sources and recovering process gases. By 2030, additional sustainable energy capacity will further lower the site’s emissions.

These investments are part of Safran Landing Systems’ broader strategy to strengthen its presence in Asia-Pacific, as illustrated by the expansion of its Singapore landing gear MRO facility, inaugurated in September 2026.

France aerospace Safran to set up first international AI subsidiary in Singapore

item.title: China offers joint AI research with Vietnam as Hanoi sets 2045 target for world-leading AI
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: China has proposed joint research on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) with Vietnam, including large language models (LLMs), open-source development and linking technology, talent and data resources, officials said at a Vietnam–China seminar on AI research and applications.
item.content:encoded:
China has proposed joint research on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) with Vietnam, including large language models (LLMs), open-source development and linking technology, talent and data resources, officials said at a Vietnam–China seminar on AI research and applications.

The seminar was held on Thursday as part of the Vietnam International Digital Week 2026, organized by Vietnam’s Ministry of Science and Technology.

Speaking at the event, Fan Bin, a deputy director in science and technology at China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, said China wants substantive cooperation with Vietnam on AI. The cooperation can cover advanced research, industrial collaboration, to open-source development, and linking innovation resources.

He said the two countries could expand cooperation in smart manufacturing, the digital economy, AI, quantum technology, and semiconductors. China is ready to share experience and help Vietnam build AI capability, including affordable and easy-to-use products, the official emphasized.

Fan Bin proposed three areas of cooperation: being a partner in open innovation, narrowing the AI gap, and developing AI for human benefit.

Vuong Thi Minh Luong, a representative of the Department of Digital Technology and AI at the Ministry of Science and Technology, said Vietnam’s national AI strategy aims to shift from research and application of AI toward a comprehensive national transformation driven by the technology.

Vietnam aims to be one of the leading centers for AI research, development, and application in Southeast Asia by 2030, and among the world’s top 10 countries in AI research, mastery and application by 2045.

Luong said Vietnam is focusing on people, data, infrastructure, governance, and product development and commercialisation. She said Vietnam wants more cooperation with China on talent, data, research and AI application. She also suggested stronger links between enterprises, research institutes, and universities.

Vietnam to add AI lessons across general education from next academic year

item.title: Roblox names Joel Neoh managing director for Southeast Asia, Oceania
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Roblox, the immersive gaming and creation platform, has appointed Joel Neoh as managing director for Southeast Asia and Oceania.
item.content:encoded:
Roblox, the immersive gaming and creation platform, has appointed Joel Neoh as managing director for Southeast Asia and Oceania.

In a statement on Friday, Roblox said Neoh joined the company in October and will be its senior-most business lead in the two regions, overseeing its strategy there and working with local teams and partners.

Neoh’s priorities will include growing the company’s presence in the region, building partnerships, and supporting the creator community. He will help local studios use Roblox’s tools to scale and find commercial success. He will also work to familiarize players and parents with the brand.

Roblox said the region’s young, digitally native population, focus on safety, and fast-changing digital ecosystem make it a significant long-term opportunity.

Neoh said he had seen the creativity, optimism, and entrepreneurial energy of the region first-hand. Technology can make it easier for people to move from consuming digital experiences to creating them. He said keeping young people safe and working with parents, regulators, and communities would remain central to the role.

Zhen Fang, Roblox’s vice president of international, said Southeast Asia and Oceania are important regions within Asia-Pacific, with a vibrant and fast-growing community of creators and players. The company is committed to the region for the long term and will keep investing in local teams, creators, and partners.

Neoh is an entrepreneur and investor with two decades of experience building technology companies across Asia-Pacific. He founded GroupsMore in Malaysia, which merged with Groupon; and Fave, a Southeast Asian fintech and consumer payments platform that Pine Labs acquired in 2021.

Roblox launches age-based Kids and Select accounts globally, expands parental controls

item.title: Indonesia rises to third in Cloudflare DDoS target ranking
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Cloudflare ranked Indonesia third among DDoS target locations in Q3 2026 as short, low-bandwidth attacks surged across its network.
item.content:encoded:
Indonesia rose to third place among the locations most targeted by distributed denial-of-service attacks in the third quarter of 2026, according to Cloudflare’s latest DDoS threat report.

The country accounted for 2.93 percent of attacks in Cloudflare’s ranking, behind the United States and China. Vietnam remained in the global top 10 at ninth place, down from seventh in the previous quarter.

The ranking reflects attacks observed and mitigated across Cloudflare’s network. It should not be read as a measure of attacks against Indonesia as a state. Under Cloudflare’s methodology, target-country data is grouped by customers’ billing countries, and the ranking combines application-layer and network-layer attack indicators, including attack volumes and the share of malicious traffic.

Short attacks rise sharply

Cloudflare said it automatically mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks during the July-to-September quarter, equivalent to about 8,226 attacks an hour. It also recorded 14.4 trillion HTTP DDoS requests.

Mitigated traffic totaled 272.6 petabytes at the network layer and 95.1 petabytes at the HTTP layer. These totals describe traffic handled by Cloudflare’s infrastructure rather than losses, outages or attempted attacks measured across the entire internet.

The network-layer attack count increased 208 percent from the same period a year earlier. Nearly 96 percent of those attacks ended within 10 minutes, while 98 percent stayed below one gigabit per second.

Cloudflare said the combination of short duration, modest bandwidth and high frequency was consistent with DDoS-for-hire services, sometimes called booter services. These services allow customers to pay for automated attacks intended to overwhelm a website, server or internet service.

The company cautioned that an attack below one gigabit per second can still disrupt a server or website, particularly when the target has limited capacity or faces repeated bursts. Cloudflare’s figures cover attacks detected by its systems and do not represent an independently audited count of all DDoS activity worldwide.

Largest attacks decline

While the total number of network-layer attacks climbed, attacks exceeding one terabit per second fell to 251 in the third quarter from 805 in the second quarter, a decline of nearly 69 percent.

Cloudflare said the decline coincided with law enforcement action earlier in the year against four large internet-of-things botnets: Aisuru, KimWolf, JackSkid and Mossad. The report presented the enforcement action as a possible factor rather than proof of direct causation.

In March, the U.S. Justice Department said it had joined authorities in Canada and Germany in disrupting command-and-control infrastructure used by the four botnets. Court documents cited by the department said the networks had infected millions of devices and launched hundreds of thousands of attacks.

Cloudflare nevertheless said internet-of-things botnets remained a significant threat as new variants emerged. Traffic it classified as Mirai-related peaked in August at 57.23 petabytes and included a sustained attack lasting 49.7 hours from August 19 to August 21.

Attack techniques shift

The report also recorded a sharp change in attack methods. Connectionless Lightweight Directory Access Protocol floods fell 99.5 percent from the second quarter and represented 0.05 percent of network-layer attacks in the third quarter.

DNS amplification attacks rose 215 percent and accounted for 3.43 percent of network-layer attacks. Other User Datagram Protocol floods increased from 14.06 percent to 31.31 percent of the total.

Both DNS amplification and other UDP-based floods can exploit connectionless protocols to direct large volumes of traffic toward a target. The rapid change between techniques suggests attackers can shift to alternative tools when a particular method becomes less effective or more exposed.

Media, production and publishing remained the most-attacked industry in Cloudflare’s data, although its share fell to about one-quarter of its second-quarter level. Internet businesses rose to sixth place, while consumer services climbed to eighth.

More than 40 Indonesian agencies hit by cyberattack on data centers – report
